children.category: stub, placeholder, or no computed result
children.description: Body produces no meaningful task computation: pass/TODO, docstring-only, unused/missing return, constant placeholder, tautological predicate, commented draft, or truncation.

children.category: missing return path or abandoned accumulator
children.description: Execution falls off the end, or an initialized result/counter/seed is never returned, or only a dead/partial branch returns, so required output is absent.

children.category: premature or first-match selection before full scan
children.description: A terminal return/index fires on first or local hit where extremal, last-occurrence, full-scan, or tie-aware selection is required; later candidates never examined.

children.category: wrong task, substituted procedure, or spec read at wrong granularity
children.description: Coherent algorithm for a different task, substituted goal, or spec term read at wrong granularity/domain/composition, giving semantically unrelated output.

children.category: required conjunct, predicate, filter, or transformation stage dropped
children.description: Correct skeleton omits a required scope predicate/conjunct, guard, parity/domain filter, or processing/reconstruction stage, silently solving a simpler or raw problem.

children.category: wrong recursive structure, base, or termination
children.description: Recursive/iterative definition models wrong ordering/nesting, or base value, termination test, argument shrinking, or call direction is wrong, producing wrong results or nontermination.

children.category: undefined name, phantom helper, or missing import
children.description: References a name/helper/module/data shape never defined or imported, or invents an API, guaranteeing NameError or fabricated-field failure independent of algorithm.

children.category: wrong tokenization, operand extraction, or unit of analysis
children.description: Parses with wrong delimiter/type/index, splits on wrong composite boundary, or treats surface tokens where semantic entities are defined, so the unit of analysis is wrong before computation.

children.category: presence vs multiplicity counting or wrong dedup rule
children.description: Counts each item once where multiplicity matters, deduplicates by set where frequency-aware removal/singleton filtering required, or relies on non-overlapping str.count/set equality.

children.category: wrong scan position, order, stride, direction, or index scope
children.description: Loop range, slice bound, start index, stride, or traversal direction is misaligned: first vs last, wrong span, overlapping skipped, positions not interleaved, or local window where prefix aggregate required.

children.category: wrong sort key, direction, extremum, or selection representation
children.description: Sorts/compares wrong collection, uses wrong key or fixed direction where condition-dependent, selects wrong extremum, or returns wrong representation of sorted data.

children.category: wrong operator, formula, metric, or comparison operand in a branch
children.description: Recognizable strategy mostly correct, but one branch operator/multiplier/formula or chosen quantity/operand is wrong, systematically breaking that case.

children.category: hardcoded cases, literal parameters, fixed/fallback result, or overfit to examples
children.description: Branches on small input set, reassigns parameters to literals, returns fixed/degenerate value, or matches a doctest/sample rather than the general rule, masking defects.

children.category: missing or wrong boundary/edge guard or invented precondition
children.description: Boundary input (empty, singleton, k==0, no letters, zero, a==b) lacks a branch/length guard causing crash or invalid result, or an unstated precondition rejects valid inputs.

children.category: wrong constant domain, character set, or case handling
children.description: Lookup/filter mechanism sound but embedded constant set is incomplete/misdefined, or handles only one case where both required, so required characters/inputs mishandled.

children.category: boundary comparison off at equality or seed value
children.description: Relational guard uses wrong comparison at equality, or exact half-way/inclusive/singleton/tie/seed rule implemented via truncation or one-directional fallback.

children.category: missing modular, sign, or rotation normalization
children.description: Raw shift/offset/sign used without required modulo, wraparound, or sign normalization, or residue constants misplaced, so cyclic/alphabet-boundary/negative inputs come out wrong.

children.category: missing secondary sort or tie-break rule
children.description: Primary filtering/ordering correct, but specified secondary ordering (alphabetical among equal lengths) or index tie-break omitted; stable sort masks the omission.

children.category: violated stated constraint, efficiency rule, or unfaithful validation
children.description: Violates explicit non-functional constraint/efficiency requirement, or validates format with unanchored/wrong-class pattern or missing length/count check, accepting malformed or rejecting valid input.

children.category: container/API contract runtime failure or ignored parameter
children.description: Assumes a container/API contract that fails at runtime (mask on list, most_common on array, sort on tuple, int on empty), or a capacity/state parameter is unused, shadowed, or rebound.

children.category: inverted, tautological, or wrong-polarity condition
children.description: Condition flipped, always true/false, imposes no constraint, tests complement/inverse of specified relation, or routes branches wrongly, yielding anti-correct behaviour.

children.category: type, conversion, or representational level confusion
children.description: Operands/types/levels conflated or required casts omitted: strings used as numbers/chars, list vs scalar arithmetic, multi-char strings treated as single chars, numeric strings not normalized.

children.category: wrong return format, shape, or destructive input mutation
children.description: Value computed but returned in wrong type/length/tuple packing/delimiter/scale, or function mutates/normalizes input destructively, losing order, case, sign, or multiplicity later needed.

children.category: missing word/neighbor boundary or single regex cannot express contract
children.description: Tests a single element where relation to neighbor/delimiter required (bare startswith, last char alone), or chosen control structure/single regex cannot represent per-side, tiered, nested conditions.

children.category: under-specified equality, wrong predicate rule, or one-sided predicate
children.description: Tests weaker pairwise/per-item property instead of exact equality/global uniformity, or uses wrong parity/digit/bound predicate, so mixed or one-sided cases wrongly accepted/counted.

children.category: incomplete permutation/rotation coverage or unnormalized comparison
children.description: Checks only truncated subset of symmetric orientations (one rotation, one hypotenuse assignment, reversed args) or compares unnormalized operands, so other orientations or numeric-string inputs fail.

children.category: docstring example or spec contradicts code
children.description: Retained doctest/example or docstring is inconsistent with what code returns or raises, or spec internally inconsistent, showing examples not reconciled with implementation.

children.category: no verifiable defect or implementation is correct
children.description: The incorrect implementation cannot be shown to be defective from the supplied material: it matches the ground truth in behaviour, the task itself is contradictory or under-specified, or the difference is only stylistic. Used only after comparing task, implementation and ground truth.
